items.prose: A chatbot says £8,000 invested at 6% a year, compounded, for 4 years grows to £9,920.

parts.question: Estimate first. Four years at 6% add 24% if nothing compounds. Where should the true balance land?

options.text: A little above £9,920, since each year's 6% is on a bigger sum
Exactly on £9,920, the figure the chatbot gave
options.why: That is the simple-interest figure. Compounding adds a little more.
With a positive rate, compounding adds to the simple figure, never takes away.
Doubling at 6% takes about 12 years, not 4.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Recall growth on growth.

explain.text: Simple interest adds 24% of £8,000, giving £9,920. Compounding adds interest on interest, so the true figure is a little above that.

parts.question: Using part 1's band, recompute exactly: £8,000 at 6% a year, compounded, for 4 years. Give the balance to the nearest penny.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply by 1.06 four times.

byKey.simple: That is the chatbot's simple-interest figure. Multiply by 1.06 each year.
byKey.three-years: You multiplied by 1.06 three times. Four years need four.

explain.text: Multiplying by 1.06 four times gives $8000 \times 1.06^4 = 10099.82$, a little above £9,920 as the estimate said.

parts.question: Taking the exact balance from part 2, how far short was the chatbot's £9,920? Give the gap in pounds, to the nearest penny.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the chatbot's figure from the exact one.

byKey.interest: That is all the interest earned. The gap is between the exact balance and £9,920.
byKey.sign: The size of the gap is positive: the chatbot was £179.82 short.

explain.text: The exact balance minus the chatbot's figure is $10099.82 - 9920 = 179.82$. It is short by the interest on interest that simple interest leaves out.

parts.question: Looking back at parts 1 to 3, which check did what?

options.text: The estimate showed £9,920 was too low; the recomputation gave the right figure
The estimate alone gave the right figure
options.why: The estimate gave a direction and a band, not the exact balance.

options.text: Only the recomputation mattered; the estimate added nothing
options.why: The estimate flagged the figure as too low before any exact sum.

options.text: Asking the chatbot "Are you sure?" would have done both
options.why: Its reply is likely text, not a check.

feedback.correct: The estimate flagged it; the recomputation fixed it.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Recall what each check gave you.

explain.text: The estimate said the answer must be a little above £9,920, so the chatbot's figure was suspect at once. The exact recomputation then gave £10,099.82.

parts.question: Start the check. What is 10% of £6,400, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. 10% is the amount divided by 10.

byKey.one: That is 1%. 10% is ten times as much.

parts.question: Using £640 for 10%, build 13% of £6,400. What is it, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. 1% is £64, so 3% is £192.

byKey.bot: That is the chatbot's figure. Build 13% from 10% and 3%.
byKey.three-of-640: You took 3% of £640. The 3% is of £6,400: £192.

parts.question: Using £832 from part 2, how much too high was the chatbot, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the right figure from the chatbot's.

byKey.sign: The size of the gap is positive: £320 too high.

explain.text: The chatbot's £1,152 minus the right £832 is £320.

parts.question: The chatbot's £1,152 is some other percentage of £6,400. Which one?

byKey.gap: That is the gap of £320 as a share of £6,400. The question asks what £1,152 is.
byKey.thirteen: 13% was asked for; the chatbot's figure is something else.

explain.text: Dividing gives $1152 / 6400 = 0.18$, so the chatbot's figure is 18%, not 13%. The ten-and-three build found it.

items.prose: A chatbot is asked the yearly cost of a 1.5% monthly charge on a £2,000 card balance left unpaid for a year, compounding monthly. It shows its working.

lines: You: What does a 1.5% monthly charge cost over a year on £2,000, compounding monthly? Show your working.
params.title: An invented example

parts.question: Tap the step that goes wrong.

feedback.correct: Step 1 adds the twelve monthly charges instead of compounding them.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask how monthly charges combine.

byKey.l3: Step 2 is arithmetic on step 1's rate; the slip is in the rate itself.

explain.text: Each month's 1.5% is on a balance that already includes earlier charges, so the rates multiply. Step 1 added them.

parts.question: Using what part 1 found, work out the true yearly rate. Give a percentage to 2 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply by 1.015 twelve times, then take off 1.

byKey.added: That is step 1's 18%, the slip part 1 found.

explain.text: Twelve months multiply the balance by $1.015^{12} \approx 1.1956$, so the yearly rate is 19.56%.

parts.question: Using the unrounded rate, $1.015^{12} - 1$, what does the year cost on £2,000, to the nearest penny?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply £2,000 by the unrounded rate.

byKey.bot: That is the chatbot's £360, built on the added 18%.
byKey.balance: That is the balance after a year. The cost is the charge alone.
byKey.rounded: You used the rounded 19.56%. Keep the full rate: £391.24.

explain.text: The charge is $2000 \times (1.015^{12} - 1) = 391.24$, using the unrounded rate. Rounding the rate to 19.56% first gives £391.20, so keep the full figure.

parts.question: Taking £391.24 from part 3, how much did the chatbot understate the cost, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the chatbot's figure from the right one.

byKey.sign: The size of the gap is positive: £31.24 understated.

explain.text: The right cost, £391.24, minus the chatbot's £360 is £31.24. The shown working let you find the one step that caused it.
